correctness.rationale: A tau-invariant collision-free unordered configuration is a disjoint union of an occupied subset T of m fixed midpoints and b free 2-orbits, each uniquely represented by one particle on the A-side open m-star, with a+2b=k. Midpoint occupancy is locally constant in the invariant collision-free locus, giving an actual clopen disjoint-union homeomorphism rather than just equality of Euler characteristics. Strictly increasing branchwise deformation identifies half-open and closed-star configuration homotopy types. Farley–Sabalka radial-tree Morse result bounds UConf_b(star) by a graph with free fundamental group. Standard subdivision and matching-polynomial Euler calculations yield chi_b=C(b+m-1,m-1)-(m-1)C(b+m-2,m-1); hence R_m(b)=1-chi_b. Binomial choices of T and b=(k-a)/2 give integral torsion-free Betti sums and generating functions. Separate arithmetic tested R_m(b)>=0 and R_m(b)>0 iff b>=2 for 3<=m<=8, 0<=b<=11. The first fixed-space nonzero H1 is therefore k=4, for all m>=3. No finite test replaces exact orbit-sector homeomorphism.
